entries:
Alpha 1.0.21 (comfort without losing the view)

  • Settings made for your hands: Phone Settings has readable Screen, Play, Sound and Device sections, larger touch controls and saved reading positions. Categories and Close stay reachable while the settings scroll.
  • Larger words, the same world: Phone menu text can grow from 100% to 125% without changing camera zoom or graphics resolution. The preference is separate from desktop UI scale and applies to the readable bag, item details, quest, journal and build-menu text.
  • Chat stays within reach: Opening phone Settings replaces the pause menu. The permanent chat strip stays clear; expanding chat closes Settings so the composer is usable, including after rotation.
  • Start at the intended brightness: A missing brightness preference now uses the documented 50% default instead of being read as zero. An explicitly saved 0% setting remains unchanged.
  • Preferences stay yours: Touch checks cover text size, graphics, sound, auto-loot, rotation, chat and saved preferences. Physical-phone sessions, remaining menus and the full mobile-playability gate are still open.

Alpha 1.0.20 (a build you can read)

  • Enemies stay selectable over loot: A living enemy under your pointer takes priority over overlapping drops, so attack clicks and deliberate phone target taps no longer become unintended pickup attempts. Clear loot remains clickable, and phone Use and auto-loot still collect nearby items.
  • Room to understand your build: Phone Skills, Talents, Runes and Combos use readable cards and larger controls above the permanent chat strip. Section buttons stay reachable while you scroll, and returning to a section preserves your reading position.
  • Read first, choose deliberately: Specialization, talent ranks and rune changes have explicit buttons. Reading a description no longer spends a talent point. Talent reset asks for confirmation; shared build state is never changed optimistically by the phone menu.
  • Find the rune you need: An ability picker narrows the rune list to one skill, with clear level requirements and Equip or Remove actions. The menu explains that specialization skills unlock automatically by level; existing progression rules are unchanged.
  • Know when a change is confirmed: Build actions wait for a matching server receipt and authoritative state. Rejected requests show feedback in the panel. Reconnect waits for a fresh build snapshot and never automatically replays an interrupted action.
  • The phone redesign continues: Desktop skill-tree interactions remain available. Remaining menus, physical-device ergonomics, sustained performance and the wider mobile milestone still require verification.

Alpha 1.0.19 (a story you can settle into)

  • Room to read Ilyra's story: Phone quest conversations and the journal use readable panels above the permanent chat strip, with larger text, scrolling lore and comfortable tracking controls.
  • Your choice, then her reply: Accept, Complete and Continue stay reachable while you scroll. Rewards still require manual completion and the server's reply; rejected requests show an error beside the action and allow a deliberate retry.
  • Arrive together: Fresh movement after recall or respawn no longer waits behind the old one-second recovery guard. This fixes reaching Ilyra on your screen while the server still sees you at the town spawn; stale movement from before recovery remains rejected.
  • Keep your place: Progress updates preserve open lore, journal reading position and tracking focus. Returning from a daily contract restores your place in the offers.
  • Every selected quest, less clutter: The phone tracker shows one compact objective with Journal and Next quest controls. Cycle all your chosen quests without changing which ones are tracked; desktop keeps its scrolling tracker.
  • A tested chapter, more work ahead: Touch checks cover long journals and a real-server first-chapter acceptance, normal combat credit, manual turn-in, gold/XP and reconnect. Physical-phone sessions, remaining menus and full campaign verification remain open.

Alpha 1.0.18 (a bag made for your hands)

  • Read your bag at a glance: Phone inventory uses scrolling item rows with icons, names and readable metadata. Bag and equipment panels use the available screen instead of shrinking desktop windows; chat keeps its small strip below them.
  • Inspect first, choose an action: Tapping bag items or equipped gear opens a dedicated detail screen. Quest materials can be inspected too. Equip and Unequip are explicit actions, so tapping gear to read it no longer removes it.
  • Compare without a keyboard: Compare shows the equipment slot a new item would replace, including ring and trinket choices. Landscape comparisons sit side by side; Back returns to your bag position.
  • A deliberate way to drop: Drop Stack asks for confirmation and rechecks the item and quantity before requesting a server drop. Changed slots cannot discard another item, quest items stay protected, and normal desktop drag-out remains available.
  • Touch flows stay under test: Phone checks cover scrolling, readable details, server-authoritative equip/unequip, canceled and confirmed drops, manual recovery and persistence. Remaining menu reflow and physical-phone playtesting are still planned.

Alpha 1.0.17 (your next step is yours)

  • Movement takes the lead: Moving the phone joystick cancels old attack and spell approaches before they move your character. Releasing it does not resume the abandoned pursuit, and your selected enemy stays selected.
  • Two thumbs, one intent: Starting movement clears older queued casts once. You can still request a new skill with your other thumb while moving; movement does not repeatedly erase those new inputs.
  • A stick that stays with your finger: A second finger cannot steal or release the active joystick. Canceled touches, focus loss and input resets return the knob to center and prevent stale touches from restarting movement.
  • Phone verification continues: Portrait and landscape real-server checks cover moving while casting, selected-target damage and manual cancellation of pursuit. Full menu reflow, all-class touch combat and physical iOS/Android playtesting remain open.

Alpha 1.0.16 (choose your mark)

  • Tap to choose, then attack: Phone taps select an enemy without starting combat. Attack and offensive skills honor that selection instead of silently choosing a closer enemy. The gold ring and compact target card stay with your chosen target.
  • Pick an enemy out of the crowd: Repeated taps cycle overlapping enemy hitboxes. Selection respects active enemies and PvP hostility, and clears when the target dies, disappears or belongs to a previous instance.
  • Cancel with a clear action: Tap empty ground or the target card's large × button to clear selection, pursuit and buffered abilities. NPC and loot taps still interact normally. A selected enemy outside cast range produces feedback instead of redirecting the spell; unselected directional skills cast ahead, while self-centered skills retain their behavior.
  • Gestures do not start fights: Selection happens on a short canvas tap's release. Dragging, pinching, canceled gestures, backgrounding and scene resets cannot turn into a selection or synthetic attack. Touch Help explains the new controls.
  • Touch combat verification expands: A real-server Wizard route checks selection, spell damage, basic attacks and cancellation in portrait and landscape. Full touch aiming, movement/pursuit refinement, menu reflow and physical-phone testing remain open.

Alpha 1.0.15 (a wider view of Eidolon)

  • A phone-sized view of the world: The camera now frames the shorter screen edge consistently. Portrait has more encounter space at default zoom; landscape characters are larger than with the old desktop framing. Rotating preserves world scale and your chosen zoom level.
  • The hero stays clear of persistent controls: Phone framing accounts for the navigation row and hotbar. Opening chat or menus does not recenter the world, and desktop camera framing is unchanged.
  • Reset without a keyboard: The phone Menu has a Reset Camera action that restores default zoom and locks the camera back onto your character. Pinching updates the view without reallocating the rendering buffer.
  • Measured, not finished: Rendered production characters and warning edges are checked alongside a real-server touch route. Full touch-combat tuning, menu reflow and real iOS/Android playtesting remain required; the mobile and 1.1 milestones are still open.

Alpha 1.0.14 (room for your thumbs)

  • Phone controls have their own space: Health bars, labeled navigation, the joystick, action buttons and hotbar no longer pile on top of one another. Portrait and landscape use different arrangements, and primary touch targets no longer shrink below 44 pixels in landscape.
  • Chat stays present without filling the screen: On phones, an always-visible strip shows new activity and opens readable history and composing controls. Collapse returns to the strip; chat never disappears. Desktop chat sizing is preserved.
  • Pinch the world, not the menus: Zoom gestures belong to the game canvas. Menu, minimap and mixed control touches cannot zoom the world; canceled or replaced fingers clear the gesture. Zoom follows finger distance instead of touch-event frequency.
  • Menus stay reachable: The phone Menu includes Skills & Runes and Abilities. Close buttons have larger hit areas, and the minimap now shares the HUD's layer so it cannot cover inventory and other menu controls.
  • Phone verification has begun: A real-server touch route checks movement and core menus in portrait and landscape. Camera framing, full menu redesign, touch combat and physical-device performance remain in progress; this is not the completed mobile or 1.1 milestone.

Alpha 1.0.13 (hold the whirlwind)

  • Whirlwind lasts through its spin: Multiplayer Whirlwind now deals its damage over two pulses in one second instead of one instant hit. Extended doubles the duration and pulse count while halving damage per pulse, preserving the cast's raw damage budget.
  • Every pulse checks its target: Moving enemies must still be within reach, in your instance and reachable through dungeon walls. Bloodwhirl healing and Bladestorm pulls apply once per enemy per cast. Death, disconnection and scene changes stop the spin.
  • The tempest travels with you: Local and remote Whirlwind effects follow the caster and use the server's remaining duration. Late observers see the remaining spin, rejected predictions clear, and the final snapshot no longer creates a brief extra flash.
  • Built in the open: The login screen quietly identifies Eidolon as an open-source project and links to its GitHub repository in a new tab.
  • Dungeon verification continues: Base and Extended casts are checked through ordinary controls at High and Low quality. The full all-class, party and campaign dungeon milestone remains open.

Alpha 1.0.12 (a clear line of fire)

  • Directional attacks respect walls: Flame Whip, Scorch Beam, Radiant Strike, Shield Slam, Sweeping Strike and Earthshaker no longer damage or debuff enemies through solid dungeon walls. Open doorways remain valid attack paths.
  • Pulls stay on the floor: Grip requires a reachable enemy before spending mana or starting its cooldown. Grip and Whirlwind's Bladestorm pull cannot overshoot a nearby enemy through the caster or into a wall.
  • Hostile auras respect cover: Whirlwind, Executioner Spin, Guardian Roar's taunt, Juggernaut Charge, Death Spiral, Smoke Bomb, Frost Nova, Heaven's Trumpet and Spirit Guardians check dungeon walls before affecting enemies. Bloodwhirl heals only from reachable hits; existing friendly buffs and healing retain their rules.
  • Scorch Beam shows its actual reach: Its beam extends beyond a nearby cursor to its full range and ends at a solid dungeon wall. Local and remote beam meshes use the same rule at High and Low quality, and the server publishes the clipped endpoint.
  • Dungeon verification continues: Ordinary Wizard casts verify beam geometry against accepted server events. Full dungeon, party, rune-duration and wider area-effect presentation checks remain open; this update does not mark the 1.1 milestone complete.
